title: Reshape the implementer prompt template and warm-chain variant
description:
Reshape the "Implementer prompt template" and "Warm-chain prompt variant" in skills/ticks/references/agent-runner.md. Those two sections only; T1 already defined the gates elsewhere in the file.

Replace the numbered Instructions step list with four parts: criteria (the acceptance), gates (the tick gate, with the by-path rule), boundaries, and report shape. Keep the following in substance:
- the IMPORTANT FIRST STEP base check
- the self-provisioning instruction (agent-runner "Provisioning" and claude-runner.md rely on it)
- the read-inputs lines (.tick/learnings.md, .tick/config.md Testing and Rules, the harness instruction file)
- the commit protocol `tick <tick-id>: <summary>`
- the Boundaries section
- the four STATUS lines

Make these changes:
- Add "do not regenerate shared generated outputs; the integrator does that once after the merge".
- Replace "implement test-first: write the failing test" with the conditional planted-fault rule (same wording as tick-patterns.md's TDD section).
- Add to the report one line per mandated check, each reading: ran clean / went red and changed the code / not applicable. A later epic's steering-sunset retro step tallies these lines, so keep the three outcomes literal.
- Give the warm-chain variant the same shape: gates and check lines per tick, one status line per tick as today.

Do NOT change the learnings path, the static-prefix order, or ledger lines; a later epic owns those.

Spec (source of truth): docs/thoughts/2026-11-12-lean-epics.md. Edit only files under skills/ticks/ (never an installed copy). Settled names, use exactly: the "tick gate" (per tick, in the worktree, run by the implementer: typecheck, the tests the change reaches, the build) and the "wave gate" (per wave, or per chain integration, run by the integrator: the full suite, slow suites, specs, shared generated outputs regenerated once). The existing in-worktree/post-merge "venues" stay: a venue says where a test tier is safe to run; the gates say who runs what, when. Add no new config syntax: `## Testing` may group commands under the two gate names in prose; the project maps commands to gates. Keep the engine voice: terse, no step lists where a criterion will do.
